title: AFP: US arms sale, military financing to boost PH defense posture, modernization
summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Friday said the continued military assistance of the United States would help strengthen Manila's defense capabilities and support its modernization…

blocks.text: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) on Friday said the continued military assistance of the United States would help strengthen Manila's defense capabilities and support its modernization efforts.

AFP spokesperson Colonel Francel Margareth Padilla issued the statement following the White House's announcement of approved foreign military financing (FMF) for the Philippines' critical defense capabilities worth over $2-billion. America will also provide $400 million in FMF for the Philippines' maritime defense in the South China Sea.
"We appreciate the continued support of the United States in strengthening the AFP's capabilities," Padilla said.
"These forms of assistance contribute to our ongoing modernization and efforts to develop a credible defense posture," she added.
The AFP's statement indicates a total US assistance package worth more than $5 billion, covering weapons sale and increased military financing.

For now, the AFP is prioritizing the procurement of kinetic capabilities and equipment to strengthen the country's territorial defense amid the presence of Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Navy vessels in Philippine waters.
In an ambush interview, AFP chief General Antonio Nafarrete said, "We concentrate now on kinetic, 'yung mga kinetic na requirement natin (those our kinetic requirements)."

"Basically for territorial defense talaga, ensuring that kapag may mga, kasi ito ano natin archipelagic, pumapasok na 'yung mga PLA na mga naval vessels dito sa sea lines of communications natin, that's international kasi so we must be able to have that deterrent capability para malaman nila na hindi basta-bastang ano rito."

(Basically for territorial defense, ensuring that when there are, because this is our archipelagic territory, PLA naval vessels enter our sea lines of communications, that's international, so we must be able to have that deterrent capability so they know it is not easy.)
Padilla stressed that any acquisition would undergo the appropriate assessment and procurement processes based on the AFP's operational requirements and national defense priorities.

Through the $400-million FMF, the AFP should be able to expand its operational reach and deterrence capabilities in the South China Sea, particularly in territorial waters that overlap with the West Philippine Sea.
The assistance is expected to cover long-range fires, command-and-control systems, critical infrastructure, and multi-domain drones.

Meanwhile, the White House said the Department of National Defense (DND) had agreed to a $37-million contract with a US firm for super intelligence-enabled mission support, and a $63-million initiative to modernize its defense cloud infrastructure for super intelligence applications. — VDV, GMA News
